title: Correct initial flux
description: Essential: Student calculates Φ₁ = BS cosθ = 0.6 × 0.4 × cos60° = 0.12 Wb.

title: Correct final flux
description: Essential: Student calculates Φ₂ after 120° rotation, recognizing the new angle between B and the coil's normal is 0° (Φ₂ = BS = 0.24 Wb).

title: Correct flux change
description: Essential: Student correctly computes ΔΦ = |Φ₂ - Φ₁| = 0.36 Wb (or equivalent signed magnitude).

title: Angle interpretation
description: Important: Student correctly interprets the given θ = 60° as the angle between the coil plane and horizontal, and relates it to the angle between B and the coil's normal (initially 30° or 150°).

title: Rotation analysis
description: Important: Student analyzes the 120° clockwise rotation to determine the new orientation of the coil relative to the vertical B-field.

title: Flux formula application
description: Important: Student applies Φ = B·A = BA cosα correctly, where α is the angle between B and the area vector.

title: Sign convention error
description: Pitfall: Student uses wrong sign convention for flux change (e.g., subtracts in wrong order) or misinterprets 'change' as final value only.

title: Angle confusion
description: Pitfall: Student incorrectly uses θ = 60° directly in cosθ for the initial flux, or misinterprets the rotation angle.

title: Units and symbols
description: Optional: Student includes proper units (Wb) and shows clear symbolic working before substitution.
